hierarchy.note: Highest structural division. DEL PRIV / ДЕЛ ПРВО or DEL I — ordinal or Roman normalised to Arabic for eId (part_1, part_2). Uncommon except in large codes.
Main structural division. GLAVA I / ГЛАВА I — Roman numerals normalised to Arabic (chp_1, chp_2). Most common higher division in primary legislation.
Mid-level division below Glava. Higher division only — NOT the basic unit. Оддел 1, Оддел 2.

BASIC UNIT. Continuous Arabic numbering throughout entire act regardless of higher divisions. Written 'Член 1', 'Член 5' in Cyrillic; 'Člen 1' in Latin. Never resets per chapter or part. Cited as 'членот X од овој закон'.
(1), (2), (3). Numbered when two or more stavovi exist in an article. Single-stav articles typically have no (1) marker.
1), 2), 3) or a), b), c) — lettered or numbered items within a stav. At least two required in practice.
Unnumbered sub-point within a tochka. Marked by dash or indent. Maps to AKN alinea.

constitution.note: Constitution of Republic of North Macedonia adopted 17 November 1991. Amended 2001 (Ohrid Framework Agreement implementation — minority rights, decentralisation, Albanian language status). Amended 2019 (Prespa Agreement — name change from 'Republic of Macedonia' to 'Republic of North Macedonia'). FRBR URI uses 1991 enactment year; amendments are expressions.

structuring.prompt_additions: North Macedonian legislation uses ARTICLE (Член / Člen) as the basic unit — NOT SECTION. SECTION (Оддел / Oddel) is only a higher division above articles. Article numbering is continuous throughout the entire act and never resets per chapter or part. Articles are written 'Член 1', 'Член 5' in Cyrillic (primary script for Macedonian legislation). Став (Stav, paragraph) is numbered (1), (2), (3) only when two or more stavovi exist; single-stav articles have no (1) marker. Точка (Tochka, point) within stavovi are numbered 1), 2) or a), b) with CLOSING PARENTHESIS only — not period-stop. Алинеа (Alineja, unnumbered sub-point) maps to ALINEA keyword. Macedonian legislation is published in Cyrillic script; OCR must handle the full Macedonian Cyrillic alphabet including Ѓ (Gje), Ѕ (Dze), Ј (Je), Љ (Lje), Њ (Nje), Ќ (Kje), and Џ (Dzhe) which differ from Serbian Cyrillic. Albanian (sqi) versions are published in Latin script for legislation affecting areas with Albanian-majority populations (≥20% threshold under the Ohrid Framework Agreement). When processing Albanian-language versions treat them as parallel FRBR expressions of the same work — not translations. The gazette promulgation header is NOT part of the enacted law — begin digitisation from the act title (ЗАКОН ЗА... / ZAKON ZA...). Cross-references cite 'Sl. vesnik na RSM' (post-2019) or 'Sl. vesnik na RM' (pre-2019) with issue and year. Amendment acts are named 'Zakon za izmenuvanye i dopolnuvanye na Zakonot za ...'. Pre-2019 laws may use 'Republika Makedonija' — preserve original text but normalise metadata to current state name.

classification_rules.note: Primary legislation (Zakon / Закон) identifiable from title — Macedonian uses 'Zakon ZA' (not 'Zakon O' as in Serbian).
Government regulations (Uredba) identifiable from title — also uses 'za' not 'o'.
Macedonian Constitution uniquely identified by title.

supranational_memberships.note: CoE member since 1995-11-09. ECHR ratified 1997. ECtHR judgments binding. Macedonian courts apply ECHR standards particularly in criminal procedure and property rights.

NATO member since 2020-03-27, following resolution of name dispute via Prespa Agreement (2018) and accession protocol ratification. 30th NATO member state. Defence and security legislation aligned with NATO standards post-accession.
OSCE member. High Commissioner on National Minorities played key role in Ohrid Framework Agreement 2001 mediation. OSCE Mission to Skopje (established 1992) monitors minority rights implementation.
CEFTA 2006 member. Regional free trade framework with Western Balkans states. Some customs and trade regulations aligned with CEFTA commitments.

EU candidate since 2005-12-17 — one of the longest-standing Western Balkans candidates. Accession negotiations formally opened March 2020 after Prespa Agreement resolved name dispute with Greece. SAA (Stabilisation and Association Agreement) in force since 2004. Does NOT yet have direct-effect EU law. Substantial acquis harmonisation already completed, particularly in trade, competition, and justice.
Observer member of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). No legal obligations.

display.note: Macedonian legislation is published in Cyrillic script as primary. Albanian co-official legislation uses Latin script. OCR must handle Macedonian Cyrillic (31 letters, differs from Serbian Cyrillic in having Ѓ, Ѕ, Ј, Љ, Њ, Ќ, Џ). Headings typically in ALL CAPS Cyrillic. Transliteration for FRBR URI slugs follows ISO 9 or BGN/PCGN romanisation conventions — document which is used during ingestion.
